newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures pare gains, end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures pare gains, end mostly higher.

text.p: CME lumber futures slipped from early short covering gains late after meeting technical resistance, closing mostly higher in generally light dealings, traders said.
Lumber closed $4.90 per tbf higher to $3.00 lower with March up $2.60 at $384.60 and May up most at $367.20 per tbf.

Futures started under pressure from the continued slow cash market, but rallied by midday on short covering paced by May. Much of the trade was considered evening up ahead of the March expiration Friday. Some stops were touched off on the rally but prices slipped late after meeting technical resistance around $371, basis May, traders said.
RBH, Saul Stone and locals bought May on the rally but Saul Stone turned seller at the high, pit sources said.

Trading was expected to be light again Friday ahead of the March expiration at noon. Part of the reduced trading interest was also attributed to the Western Wood Products Association meeting in San Francisco, which will be attended by many industry executives, they said.
